h1:
Nong Bua Lamphu in 1 Day
City + Wat Tham Klong Phen, or Phu Phan Kham
intro: Nong Bua Lamphu is a small town a lot of people just drive through on the Udon Thani–Loei road, assuming there's nothing to see. Truth is, if you've only got one day, it's an easy place to enjoy — the sights sit close together and you won't be jostling anyone for a photo. We've split it into two routes so you can pick by mood — the city + Wat Tham Klong Phen to pay respects to Luang Pu Khao, or the nature route out to Phu Phan Kham by the Ubolratana Dam.
chips: 🛕 Pay respects to Luang Pu Khao

blocks.html: The nice thing about Nong Bua Lamphu is that everything sits close together. In town you can walk over to the King Naresuan shrine beside the lake; drive less than 20 minutes out and you're at Wat Tham Klong Phen; and if you want wide water views, you can run over to the Phu Phan Kham side by the Ubolratana Dam. So we've laid out two plans to choose from. You can do one full-day plan, or take one for the morning and the other for the afternoon — the distances are short enough either way.

blocks.text: Before you set off — a few things to know

items: Your own car is by far the easiest — the sights are spread out beyond town and local public transport is thin. If you don't have a car, the move is to rent one in Udon Thani (about 45 minutes away) and drive in.
Wat Tham Klong Phen is open 08:00–17:00, no entry fee, but dress modestly — it's a meditation temple.
Starting early pays off — Isan mornings heat up by mid-morning, so if you set out before 9am you'll have a much easier time walking the temple and taking photos.
Rainy season (Jun–Oct) makes the Phu Phan Kham dam views lush and green, but pack an umbrella. Cool season (Nov–Jan) is comfortable enough to be out all day.

blocks.text: Plan A — City + Wat Tham Klong Phen

blocks.html: The classic route for a first-timer in Nong Bua Lamphu: pay your respects, stroll along the lake, then head out to Wat Tham Klong Phen, the province's highlight. Good for anyone who likes a relaxed temple day without much driving.

blocks.label: Plan A
blocks.title: City – Wat Tham Klong Phen – Café

items.activity: Start at the King Naresuan the Great shrine, beside Nong Bua public park
items.note: It sits right in the town center in front of the district office and is deeply revered by locals — people bring rooster figurines as offerings to fulfill vows. A morning walk along the lake in the breeze is just right.

items.activity: Drive out to Wat Tham Klong Phen (about 13 km via Highway 210, the Nong Bua Lamphu–Udon Thani road)
items.note: Turn off at the junction and it's roughly another 2 km to the temple at the foot of the Phu Phan range.

items.activity: Pay respects to Luang Pu Khao Analayo at Wat Tham Klong Phen, then wander the rock garden and the ancient drum cave
items.note: It's a huge temple — you can drive in. There's a museum of Luang Pu Khao's belongings and a wax figure of him, oddly shaped boulders, and quiet, shady grounds. Allow about 1–1.5 hours to walk it.

items.activity: Head back into town for lunch — try Som Tam Nayok
items.note: Their standout is the crab-and-fermented-fish som tam with crispy-skin grilled chicken — proper Isan flavors, around 100+ THB a plate.

items.activity: Take a break at Belief Cafe' & Garden
items.note: The flower garden is done up nicely with plenty of photo spots, and an iced coffee out of the afternoon sun hits the spot. Drinks run around 100 THB and up.

items.activity: Back for a stroll along Nong Bua / a stop at the souvenir market
items.note: Come evening, locals come out to walk in the breeze — an easy-going vibe, good for catching the sunset over the lake.

items.activity: Dinner with a nice atmosphere at Tree Bar & Restaurant
items.note: There's both an air-conditioned room and an outdoor zone, with live music in the evenings. Standouts: miang kham lamphu, garlic-fried fish, and young-coconut ho mok.

blocks.title: Plan A tip
blocks.html: Wat Tham Klong Phen is large with rocky rises, so wear comfortable walking shoes. The midday sun is fierce — if you want to see the whole place, go in the morning and come back into town to eat.

blocks.text: Plan B — The nature route: Phu Phan Kham by the Ubolratana Dam

blocks.html: If you're after wide water, mountains, and a cool breeze, this plan takes you out to the Phu Phan Kham side — part of Phu Kao–Phu Phan Kham National Park, which wraps around the reservoir above the Ubolratana Dam. It's a sunset spot locals like to come and sit in the wind.

blocks.label: Plan B
blocks.title: Phu Phan Kham – Ubolratana Dam – Waterside spots

items.activity: Leave town heading for the Phu Phan Kham side (Non Sang district, by the Ubolratana Dam)
items.note: It's about 40–50 km, an easy drive past fields and mountains.

items.activity: Stop at the viewpoint over the reservoir above the Ubolratana Dam, around the Phu Phan Kham park area
items.note: Wide water flanked by mountain ridges — a favorite spot around here for photos and catching the breeze.

items.activity: Wander the nature around Phu Kao–Phu Phan Kham National Park
items.note: Big stretches of forest with several viewpoints — good for anyone who likes quiet and open air.

items.activity: Lunch at a waterside spot — try Thung Na at 9Dee Café or a restaurant by the dam
items.note: Sit back in the breeze with a view over the fields. Standouts: tom yum sea bass and herb-fried mullet, with fresh fish from the nearby water.

items.activity: Keep on at a café / take more waterside photos
items.note: The afternoon sun softens — a good time to sip coffee and wait for the evening light.

items.activity: Wait for sunset over the dam
items.note: The highlight of this plan — golden light glances off the water beautifully. Leave plenty of time to sit and take in the breeze.

items.activity: Drive back into town for dinner
items.note: If you're still hungry, try Krua Parinya & Restaurant in town — the tom yum sea bass and sea bass miang are favorites.

blocks.title: Plan B tip
blocks.html: On the Phu Phan Kham side, the spots and eateries are spread out. Check the coordinates and opening hours of any waterside restaurant before you set off, since some are local places that may close on weekdays — and top up your fuel, because gas stations aren't frequent out here.

blocks.text: Can you do half and half if you want both routes?

blocks.html: Yes, and plenty of people do, because the distances aren't far. The simple formula: morning for the temple and Wat Tham Klong Phen (the temple is best walked in the morning before the sun gets harsh), then afternoon run out to Phu Phan Kham to wait for sunset over the dam, capped off with dinner in town. One day, both the merit-making and the nature. Just accept it'll be a bit more rushed, and you'll have less time at each stop.

items: 08:00–09:30 King Naresuan shrine + walk along Nong Bua
10:00–12:00 Wat Tham Klong Phen, pay respects to Luang Pu Khao
14:30–18:00 Phu Phan Kham by the Ubolratana Dam + sunset

blocks.text: What to eat during the day

items.name: Som Tam Nayok
items.blurb: An in-town som tam spot that locals vouch for. The standout is the bold crab-and-fermented-fish som tam with crispy-skin grilled chicken — perfect for lunch on a hot day.

items.name: Tree Bar & Restaurant
items.blurb: The town's good-atmosphere spot, with both an air-conditioned room and an outdoor zone, plus live music in the evenings. Try the miang kham lamphu, garlic-fried fish, and young-coconut ho mok — good for dinner.

items.name: Krua Parinya & Restaurant
items.blurb: A made-to-order restaurant where townsfolk go for a special meal. Tom yum sea bass, herb-fried mullet, and sea bass miang — a sure hand in the kitchen.

items.name: Thung Na at 9Dee Café
items.blurb: A field-side spot where you sit in the breeze with a view over the rice paddies. Standouts: tom yum sea bass and herb-fried mullet — good for the nature route out of town.

items.name: Belief Cafe' & Garden
items.blurb: A flower-garden café people share a lot, with plenty of photo spots and iced coffees and drinks — good for an afternoon break.

items.name: Sum Hua Cafe & Restaurant
items.blurb: A homey-style café pulling Thai–Isan food, drinks, and desserts together in one place. Comfortable and easygoing.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Nong Bua Lamphu is a small town — there aren't as many well-known spots as in a big city, and some local places keep irregular hours. Check the restaurant's page or call ahead to be sure. Don't expect the range of options you'd get in Chiang Mai or Khon Kaen — but the charm here is the quiet, and not having to fight anyone for a spot.

faq.q: Is one day enough for Nong Bua Lamphu?
faq.a: Comfortably, yes — it's a small town and the sights sit close together. In a day you can pick one route — the city + Wat Tham Klong Phen, or the Phu Phan Kham dam route — or do half a morning and half an afternoon to fit both, just a little more rushed.

faq.q: What are Wat Tham Klong Phen's hours, and is there an entry fee?
faq.a: It's open daily around 08:00–17:00 with no entry fee. Inside there's a museum of Luang Pu Khao's belongings and a wax figure of him, a rock garden, and the ancient drum cave. The grounds are very large and you can drive in — allow about 1–1.5 hours to walk it.

faq.q: Can you visit Nong Bua Lamphu without your own car?
faq.a: You can, but it's harder, since local public transport is thin and sights like Wat Tham Klong Phen and Phu Phan Kham are outside town. The easiest way is to rent a car in Udon Thani (about 45 minutes away) and drive in, or hire a local car by the day.

faq.q: Are Phu Phan Kham and Wat Tham Klong Phen in the same direction?
faq.a: Different directions. Wat Tham Klong Phen is toward Udon Thani (Highway 210), about 13 km from town. Phu Phan Kham, by the Ubolratana Dam, is over on the Non Sang district side, about 40–50 km away. To do both in one day, the temple in the morning and Phu Phan Kham in the afternoon for sunset works best.

faq.q: When's the best time to visit Nong Bua Lamphu?
faq.a: Cool season (Nov–Jan) is comfortable enough to be out all day. Rainy season (Jun–Oct) makes the Phu Phan Kham dam views lush and green, but bring an umbrella. Around 25 Jan–3 Feb there's the King Naresuan worship festival in town, so if you like a traditional-festival atmosphere, come then.
